names.spalding_house_1637_prairie: 1637 Prairie Avenue — Jesse Spalding's remodel of the Grosvenor house

source.citation: [South side of the Grosvenor house, 1637 S. Prairie Avenue, as built.] Photograph from the south-west across Prairie Avenue; photographer and original holder not named, c. 1870 (before Jesse Spalding's remodelling). Reproduced by the Glessner House Museum, 'The Early History of Prairie Avenue - Part IV', The Story of a House (blog), 7 July 2020.
what_it_does_not_supply: the 1904 state: it predates the remodel, so the front, the roof and the fence it shows are weighed against the engraving and the 1911 sheet, not built from it
the eave's height: the fence hides the ground, so its camera reads heights only against an assumed band (the solve)
the north flank, the rear range and the roof behind the eave
what_it_supplies: the south wall blank from the front corner to the projection, about u 12.0 to 3.9-5.2 m through its camera

the south projection's place, which the 1911 sheet's canted bay on the south wall (u 4.1 to 1.0) agrees with, and its c. 1870 dress: round-arched lights between columns, a bracketed entablature, a balcony on top before a shuttered window
a stack over the south flank at about u 6.0 (if it stands on the wall's line), its top about 14.2 m over grade
a pale stone band along the foot of the south wall
